note: GENERATED. Every record and every counter below is re-derived from the tree on each run. Nothing here is hand-maintained.

diagnostics.why: Recovers `testCallerCount` / `testOnly` from the retired route-consumers.json. Test callers are excluded from the consumer AUTHORITY on purpose — a proof suite calling a route is what makes an orphan look connected — so this may never be read to decide whether a route is wired.

retired.reason: Output of the retired TEXT consumer scanner. Its subject — which routes have a product or machine caller — is measured by the AST engine, whose per-route records carry the caller's file and line. The retired scanner's own numbers were the known-wrong half of the 773-vs-785 disagreement that FINAL-001 was opened for.

semantics.derivation: substring occurrence of a route path anywhere in a test file
semantics.quality: NOISY. A substring match counts a path that appears in a comment, in a doc string, or as a prefix of a different route's path, and misses every caller that builds its path from a template. The same scanner produced the 773-vs-785 disagreement that FINAL-001 was opened for.
semantics.whyNotReproducible: Reproducing the figures exactly would mean rebuilding the substring scanner, which is the thing Phase 0 retired. The replacement measures a different, narrower and better-defined population.

retired.uniqueDataLost: `testCallerCount` / `testOnly` per route. The canonical map does not publish a test-caller dimension, and the two cases it collapses — 'no callers at all' and 'only suites call this' — are genuinely different facts.

uniqueDataResolution.option: A — REPLACED BY A HISTORICAL DIAGNOSTIC (NOT AN EXACT RE-DERIVATION)
uniqueDataResolution.replacementSemantics: AST-resolved lower bound over test request call sites
uniqueDataResolution.semanticDifference: The old metric counted SUBSTRINGS; the new one counts RESOLVED CALLS. It therefore excludes comments, doc strings and coincidental path prefixes that the old one counted, and excludes Fastify `app.inject()` — not a request primitive — that the old one would have caught as a substring. The two numbers are not comparable in either direction, and the new one is a lower bound.
uniqueDataResolution.how: The canonical analyzer, opted into the test trees (`analyzeSources({ includeTests: true })`), resolving request primitives to routes exactly as it does for product callers. Suites live outside every product root, so the diagnostic supplies the test roots as a `product: false` tree — widening what is OBSERVED without widening what may be classified as a consumer.
uniqueDataResolution.whyNotAnAuthority: Test callers are excluded from the consumer authority on purpose: a proof suite calling a route is exactly what makes an orphan look connected. The governance gate refuses to let any gate read this file, refuses to let it claim a sourceOfTruthFor, and refuses to credit it toward product closure.

retired.reason: Regenerable output of the working-tree freeze collector.
A collector living inside the directory it wrote to, with no package script, no CI reference and no consuming gate. MOVED rather than deleted.

packageScripts.command: PHASE 0 — `audit:architecture` is the ONE current-audit command. Default regenerates every current artifact then checks the engine. `--engine-check` asks whether the measuring instrument is sound and exits 0 even while product work is open. `--closure-check` asks whether the PRODUCT is closed and exits non-zero while it is not. Keeping those apart is deliberate: a permanent red that means 'open work' teaches everyone to ignore a red that means 'every number here is a guess'.
